lines.text: ## How it works

The CLI indexes `base...head` and writes a covering skeleton `review.json`: one path per changed file, stub prose, hunk refs. The skill fills interpretation only: title, groups, summaries, attention, lookFor, sources. `validate` checks refs and coverage. `serve` and `export` share one UI and one git payload. Live git wins.

`pregroup` indexes `base...head` and writes a covering draft `review.json`: one group per repeated change, one for mechanical files, and one for the rest, with stub prose and hunk refs. The skill reads the change with `digest` and `show`, regroups the draft, and fills interpretation only. `validate` checks the schema, refs, coverage, and citations. `serve` and `export` share one UI and one git payload. Live git wins.
## Where code lives
- `skills-next/comprehende/` - skill source. The only skill text you edit.
- `.agents/skills/` - skills for agents that work in this repo. `.claude/skills` is a symlink to it, because Claude Code does not read `.agents/skills`.
- `src/schema/` - review document schema. The source of truth. Parse at the boundary, infer inside.

- `src/review/` - review-document logic behind the commands: `skeleton.ts` (`review`), `digest.ts`, `coverage.ts`, `anchors.ts`, `pins.ts` (`validate`), `refresh.ts`, `show.ts`. `pregroup` lives in `src/cli/commands.ts`.
- `src/api/` - UI payloads: `types.ts`, `changes.ts` (What changed), `agent-md.ts`, `live.ts`. A new review field passes through here.
- `src/review/` - review-document logic behind the commands. `pregroup` lives in `src/cli/commands.ts`.
- `src/api/` - UI payloads. A new review field passes through here.
- `src/cli/`, `src/server/`, `src/git/` - CLI, serve/export server, live git reads.
- `src/ui/` - fixed UI. Only the data changes.
- `eval/cases/`, `scripts/eval/` - eval cases and runner.
- `scripts/` - `fixture`, `sync-skill`, schema build.
- `scripts/` - dev, release, and Pages scripts.
A fresh worktree with no `node_modules` or `.env`: run `node scripts/setup-worktree.ts`.

Producer and grader run in Muse Code (`muse exec`). The producer defaults to `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`; the grader defaults to `muse-ember-1.0`. Override with `--producer-model` or `--grader-model`.

Muse Ember (`muse-ember-1.0`) grades by default because repeated rescore checks put it at parity for less time. It has no contributor variant, so the harness passes `--contributor-mode off` for it; with the mode on it fails with "does not exist or you lack access". Across five runs each on `comprehende-50` and `comprehende-57`, Ember-vs-Spark verdict agreement (median 50 of 52) overlapped Spark-vs-Spark (51 of 52), grader tokens matched at the median, no run failed to parse, and Ember graded about 3.7 times faster. The producer stays on Spark contributor: Ember spot checks wrote thinner reviews, and on the Model API Ember output costs $0.50 per 1M tokens against Spark contributor $0.20 (input $0.10 both; Ember bills the whole request at $0.30 input and $1.50 output over 200K input tokens).

lines.text: ## Muse setup

Runs use the `muse` CLI login (`muse login`), which spends the subscription, by default — even when `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY` is set. `--use-api-key` spends that key (pay as you go) instead. `--cli-login` names the default and wins over `--use-api-key`. CI writes the repo secret `MUSE_AUTH_JSON` (a CI-only device login, not your daily one) to `~/.config/muse/auth.json` and checks it with `muse usage`; only a missing secret falls back to `--use-api-key` with `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY` — a failed check keeps the subscription so a dead login fails visibly instead of silently spending API credit. Refresh an expired CI login by running `muse login` once in any Linux environment with a fresh `HOME` (a container works), then `gh secret set MUSE_AUTH_JSON < ~/.config/muse/auth.json`. Every Muse run resolves a bare `muse-spark-<version>` id to its `-contributor` tier and passes `--contributor-mode on` for that tier and for `muse-wonder` ids, which Muse Code offers in either mode; other ids, such as `muse-spark-1.3-turbo` and `muse-ember-1.0`, stay unchanged and get `--contributor-mode off`, because they have no contributor variant. The `muse` CLI must be on `PATH`. The eval workflow installs it. Locally, install the CLI the way `.github/workflows/eval.yml` does.

When the subscription quota runs out, each Muse call fails in seconds with `API error 429: Subscription quota exhausted` and the time the window resets. Rerun with `--use-api-key` instead of waiting for the reset. A grader that hit the quota shows only `rubric parse FAIL` and `grader 0 tok` on the case line; the error is in that case's `result.json`. When the reviews are already saved, `--rescore eval/runs/<stamp> --use-api-key` regrades them and pays for no producer.

**Review document.** Interpretation only. Title, groups, summaries, optional generated why, optional attentions, questions, focus ranges, notes, and file notes, optional lookFor, sources, hunk pointers. Never patch text. Source refs must resolve in cwd.
**Group.** Schema `groups` item. The UI uses the same word.
**Review concern.** Why these hunks are read together. Not a directory, unless that directory is the concern.
**Part / story.** Independent work. Could have been its own PR. `dependsOn` only inside a story.
**Size.** Review burden. Not file or hunk count.
**Hunk ref.** Pointer into live git. Copy from the `review` skeleton. Never invent.
**Hunk ref.** Pointer into live git. Path and directory refs come from the `pregroup` draft; the numbers of a single hunk come from the digest or `show`. Never invent.
**Index.** Internal hunk list. No line content. Not stored in the UI. `review` writes those refs into a covering skeleton.
**Index.** Internal hunk list (`HunkIndex`). No line content. Not sent to the UI. `review` writes one path per file from it; `pregroup` writes path and directory refs that cover the same hunks.
**Live git.** `git` in cwd at serve time. Git wins.

lines.text: Producer and grader run in Muse Code (`muse exec`). The producer defaults to `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`; the grader defaults to `muse-ember-1.0`. Override with `--producer-model` or `--grader-model`.

Muse Ember (`muse-ember-1.0`) grades by default because repeated rescore checks put it at parity for less time. It has no contributor variant, so the harness passes `--contributor-mode off` for it; with the mode on it fails with "does not exist or you lack access". Across five runs each on `comprehende-50` and `comprehende-57`, Ember-vs-Spark verdict agreement (median 50 of 52) overlapped Spark-vs-Spark (51 of 52), grader tokens matched at the median, no run failed to parse, and Ember graded about 3.7 times faster. The producer stays on Spark contributor: Ember spot checks wrote thinner reviews, and on the Model API Ember output costs $0.50 per 1M tokens against Spark contributor $0.20 (input $0.10 both; Ember bills the whole request at $0.30 input and $1.50 output over 200K input tokens).

A `claude-*` producer model (for example `--producer-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --producer-effort high`) runs the producer in Claude Code (`claude -p`) with the `claude` CLI login only; API key variables are removed from its environment. Use it to compare Claude models. The grader stays in Muse. With `--keep`, resume a Claude producer with `claude --resume <sessionId>` from its clone.
